Agent Instructions for sciVizModules

Source: AGENTS.md

Repository Overview

sciVizModules extends VizModules with interactivity-first Shiny modules for scientific analyses and plots. Prefer composition and extension of VizModules over parallel reimplementations of general plotting-module behavior.

Stack: R (>= 4.6.0), Shiny, VizModules (>= 0.6.0), plotly, roxygen2 | Version: 0.99.0 | License: MIT + file LICENSE

The package targets Bioconductor (see biocViews in DESCRIPTION and BIOCONDUCTOR_SUBMISSION_PLAN.md), so keep R CMD check clean and follow Bioconductor packaging conventions.

Repository Structure

  • R/ - source files: *_module_ui.R (UI), *_module_server.R (logic), *_module_app.R (examples), plus *_helpers.R and standalone plot functions. Package-wide helpers live in example_data.R, input_helpers.R, palette_helpers.R and figure_builder_registry.R. module_showcase.R holds the example-data catalogue and the showcase registry every module needs an entry in; moduleGallery_app.R builds the gallery from it (see “Adding a Module: Gallery, App and Figure Builder”)
  • man/ - Auto-generated roxygen2 docs
  • data/ - example datasets used by tests, examples, and vignettes. DESCRIPTION sets no LazyData, so package code reaches them through .sci_example_data(), never by bare name. Do not ship data a dependency already ships: read it from that package with a small internal loader (.maf_example() reads maftools’ TCGA LAML MAF, .se_example() the airway package’s counts), guard examples with requireNamespace(), and in tests use the skipping helpers in tests/testthat/helper-example-data.R
  • data-raw/ - scripts that build the example datasets
  • vignettes/ - quick-start.Rmd. Every chunk is eval = FALSE; these are Shiny apps
  • tests/testthat/ - testthat tests, plus testthat.R to run the suite
  • inst/apps/module-gallery/ - a thin app.R deploying sciModuleGalleryApp() (to shinyapps.io or Posit Connect), with its rsconnect manifest.json (build-ignored)
  • .github/workflows/ - R-CMD-check.yaml and pkgdown.yaml
  • DESCRIPTION - Package metadata and dependencies
  • NAMESPACE - Generated by roxygen2 (NEVER EDIT MANUALLY)
  • **_pkgdown.yml** - curated reference index for the docs site; every new export needs an entry
  • .lintr - Line length: 120 chars, indentation: 4 spaces
  • .Rbuildignore - Files excluded from package build

Modules In This Package

alphafoldConfidence, cnSegmentPlot, deHeatmap, dittoBarPlot, dittoDimHex, dittoDimPlot, dittoDotPlot, dittoFreqPlot, dittoHeatmap, dittoPlot, dittoRidgeJitter, dittoScatterPlot, crisprScreenRank, doseResponse, enrichmentDotPlot, forestPlot, goFanPlot, gseaEnrichmentPlot, gwasQQPlot, mafSummary, maPlot, manhattanPlot, mdTrajectoryMetrics, michaelisMenten, mutationalProfile, mutationLollipop, oncoPlot, pcaBiplot, pcaEigencorPlot, pcaLoadingsPlot, pcaPairsPlot, pcaScreePlot, pkConcentrationTime, plateHeatmap, rocCurve, sampleDistanceHeatmap, samplePCA, structureViewer, survivalCurve, volcanoPlot.

The modules that build their own plotly figure (the PCAtools family except pcaBiplot, alphafoldConfidence, gseaEnrichmentPlot, the MAF modules oncoPlot, mafSummary and mutationLollipop, and the data-frame modules forestPlot, rocCurve, pkConcentrationTime, plateHeatmap, mdTrajectoryMetrics and survivalCurve) share their server, input layout and app scaffolding through .sci_plot_server(), .sci_plot_inputs_ui() and .sci_object_app() in R/module_helpers.R; a new module of that kind should too. .sci_finalize_plotly() (R/plotly_helpers.R) applies the uniform Axes/Legend/Lines/Plotly finishing to a figure a module builds itself. It styles every axis, so a panel whose axes must keep their own settings (the risk table’s gridlines) names them in attr(fig, "fixed.axes"); and since plotly draws a shared axis’s lines on one panel only, it boxes each panel of a subplot() with shared axes through .sci_shared_panel_borders(). A panel that needs gridlines or borders of its own, independent of its neighbours, gets an x axis of its own matched to theirs (matches = "x", as survivalCurve‘s risk table does). A data-frame module passes validate = .sci_require_df and uses createModuleApp() for its app; a group-colour picker goes through setup_group_colors() plus .sci_palette_picker_ui(). A categorical colour, shape or group select takes its choices from .sci_discrete_cols() (R/input_helpers.R), a thin wrapper of VizModules’ discrete_choices() that also accepts non-data-frame metadata and, with numeric = TRUE, low-cardinality numeric columns (a dose). It keeps facet_check()‘s columns (fewer than 50 levels) plus logicals, so an ID column is never offered, and takes keep for the column a caller named in defaults, which is offered whatever its size, as in the VizModules modules. A confidence band or error bars around a line go through VizModules::linePlot() with error.type = "columns" and error.ribbon / error.bar, so the band takes its line’s colour and legend group as in the line plot module, rather than hand-built fill traces; work out a group’s half-width with VizModules::error_bar_halfwidth() (pkConcentrationTime’s group means), and draw a step function from duplicated step coordinates (survivalCurve’s .km_steps()). ggplotly() cannot convert survminer’s stepped confidence band and drops it. Statistics the module computes (AUCs, NCA parameters, plate Z’, Kaplan-Meier medians and the log-rank test) are attached to the figure as attr(fig, "table"), which .sci_plot_server() routes into the source-data download. A module with more than one table attaches a named list of them, which the download writes as one CSV each (survivalCurve’s strata summary and, while pairwise comparisons are on, its pairwise table); the plot function itself keeps a single "table" and returns the others as attributes of their own (attr(fig, "pairwise")). Pairwise tests are adjusted across the comparisons made, carry an effect size with its interval, never hide non-significant results, and come with interpretation notes in the function’s Details and the vignette. Readers for non-R tool outputs are exported read_*() functions (read_alphafold(), read_mageck(), read_structure(), read_xvg()). Where a reference package computes the same quantity (pROC, PKNCA, fgsea, survminer), compute it in-package and test it equal to that package under skip_if_not_installed(), keeping the reference in Suggests.

structureViewer is the reference for a non-plotly widget module (see Critical Rule 6). It renders the NGLVieweR widget once per structure, restyles through NGLVieweR_proxy() with named representations so the camera is kept, and builds its own control strip (Reset, PNG snapshot, structure download) because module_tack_ui() always carries the plotly Source Data button. Wrappers of the VizModules scatter module add layers through its fig.fn hook via a testable internal .<module>_layers(fig, ..., input, isolate_fn) function (see .pca_biplot_layers(), .manhattan_layers()). The scatter server draws trajectories (arrowheads as annotations), then runs fig.fn, then adds the Marginals tab’s strips with add_marginal_plots(), which shrinks the main panel and moves paper-anchored shapes and annotations into it. So a layer function appends to layout$annotations and layout$shapes rather than replacing them, and a layer on paper coordinates still lands in the panel. A wrapper whose axes are not distributions (genomic position, expected quantiles, rank, dose) hides “Marginals” by default, as manhattanPlot, gwasQQPlot, crisprScreenRank and doseResponse do.

The heatmap modules (dittoHeatmap, sampleDistanceHeatmap, deHeatmap) wrap VizModules’ ComplexHeatmap_Heatmap (non-plotly, InteractiveComplexHeatmap; ComplexHeatmap, InteractiveComplexHeatmap and circlize are Suggests) through .heatmap_wrapper_server() and friends in R/heatmap_wrapper_helpers.R; a new heatmap wrapper should too. The wrapper builds list(matrix =, column_annotations =) with .heatmap_frame() (key column first, names made unique), fixes and hides the base’s matrix.cols / rowname.col, and hands the column order to the base as a reactive matrix.cols default, since the base reads the order from that input, not the data. Things that bite: an error inside the base’s build observer ends the session, so preparation goes through .sci_soft_errors() (a validate() failure, shown in the wrapper’s status line); rows with no variance or a missing value break Pearson distances and row scaling (.heatmap_clean_rows()); column_annotations defaults must stay static (a reactive one breaks the multiDynamicInput JS); column_key cannot be hidden (it shares a grid cell with the annotation editor); and reactive defaults are isolate()d when the base server is built, so they must fall back rather than req(). The somatic-mutation modules read a maftools MAF object or a MAF data frame through .maf_table() (R/maf_helpers.R), whose summaries are tested equal to maftools’; maftools itself is needed only for protein domains.

Each exposes the *InputsUI() / *OutputUI() / *Server() / *App() set. Run the *App() to inspect one interactively, or sciModuleGalleryApp() to see them all: every module on its own tab under a menu by field, each opening on its example data with its main features switched on, and the Figure Builder. A module’s server starts only when its tab is first opened, so the gallery is the fastest way to click through every module after a change.

The data-frame modules flagged figure_builder = TRUE in the showcase registry are also offered by the VizModules Figure Builder through sci_figure_builder_registry(), which is derived from that registry, so they can be arranged into a multi-panel figure with sciFigureBuilderApp(). The dittoSeq modules (SingleCellExperiment input), the bulk expression modules samplePCA, sampleDistanceHeatmap and deHeatmap (SummarizedExperiment), cnSegmentPlot (CNSegment) and michaelisMenten (a bundle carrying a model fit), the PCAtools modules (a pca object) and alphafoldConfidence (a read_alphafold() result) cannot be registered - the builder’s dataset catalogue holds data frames - and structureViewer is not a plotly figure. forestPlot, the GWAS modules, crisprScreenRank, the MAF modules (oncoPlot, mafSummary, mutationLollipop), rocCurve, pkConcentrationTime, plateHeatmap and mdTrajectoryMetrics take a data frame but are not flagged yet.

Build and Validation

Prerequisites

DESCRIPTION declares R (>= 4.6.0). Use R 4.6.1 installation for development, build, and test.

Key R Commands

# ALWAYS run after changing roxygen2 comments or function signatures
devtools::document()          # Updates NAMESPACE and .Rd files

# Development
devtools::load_all()          # Load package for testing
devtools::check()             # Run R CMD check
devtools::check_man()         # Faster: documentation consistency only
lintr::lint_package()         # Lint code (120 char lines, 4-space indent)

# Building
devtools::build()             # Create .tar.gz
pkgdown::build_site()         # Build documentation website

# Testing
devtools::test()                                  # Whole testthat suite
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-x.R")    # Single file (much faster)
cnSegmentPlotApp()                                # Interactive testing of one module
sciModuleGalleryApp()                             # Every module, each on its showcase settings

Build Commands (Shell)

R CMD build sciVizModules                                    # Build package
R CMD check --no-build-vignettes sciVizModules_*.tar.gz      # Quick check

CI/CD

  • R-CMD-check.yaml - Runs R CMD check on push to main/master and on pull requests, across an OS/R version matrix.
  • pkgdown.yaml - Triggers on push/PR to devel/main, releases, or manual dispatch. Builds the docs website and deploys to gh-pages. Uses use-public-rspm: true for fast binary installs on Ubuntu.

Coding Conventions

VizModules Foundation

VizModules is a hard dependency (Depends: VizModules (>= 0.6.0)) and the primary foundation for generic interactive plotting, UI organization, downloads, annotations, and module infrastructure.

  • Before building or changing a module, first check whether an existing VizModules module, helper, or wrapper pattern covers the general behavior. Extend it with science-specific defaults, controls, data preparation, annotations, or validation instead of recreating it.
  • Every VizModules plot module follows the shared *InputsUI(id, ...), *OutputUI(id), and *Server(id, data = reactive(...), ...) contract. Preserve this contract when wrapping or composing a base module.
  • Use defaults to set scientific defaults. Use hide.inputs and hide.tabs to enforce fixed values without exposing the corresponding generic controls.
  • Prefer documented VizModules arguments and helpers over local replacements. Commonly useful ones, grouped by what they do:
    • Inputs and layout: organize_inputs(), module_tack_ui(), hide_input() / show_input() / toggle_input_cell(), viz_select_input() / update_viz_select(), multiColorPicker() / updateMultiColorPicker(), multiDynamicInput() / updateMultiDynamicInput(), and the uniform input blocks (uniform_axes_inputs_ui(), uniform_legend_inputs_ui(), uniform_lines_inputs_ui(), uniform_plotly_inputs_ui(), uniform_annotation_inputs_ui()) with their reset counterparts (reset_axes_inputs(), reset_legend_inputs(), reset_lines_inputs(), reset_plotly_inputs(), reset_annotation_inputs()), plus uniform_subplot_spacing_inputs_ui() / subplot_spacing_defaults() for a Facet tab’s spacing controls.
    • Defaults and server-side stores: get_default(), setup_reactive_defaults(), setup_auto_update_logic(), setup_group_colors(), setup_axis_range(), resolve_palette(), setup_manual_edits() / finalize_manual_edits() / reset_manual_edits(), and for a group colour picker default_group_colors() (validates and hex-normalises a mapping in defaults) with reset_group_colors() (restores the picker on Reset). See “Avoiding Double Renders” below.
    • Server boilerplate: require_data_frame() wraps a data-frame module’s data reactive; blank_to_null() turns a select’s "" (or NA, or a missing input) into NULL, and nz_value() tests for a usable string without erroring on NULL; with_stable_seed() builds a jittered plot under a fixed seed so the points stay put across rebuilds; facet_check(), discrete_choices() (a colour, shape, group or fill select’s categorical choices, capped at 50 levels), flatten_palette_options(), and as_plotted() / adjusted_values() / adjustment_fn() for anything drawn over an adjusted axis.
    • Plot finishing: apply_title_layout(), create_axis_styles(), apply_subplot_axis_styling(), axis_titles_as_annotations(), apply_axis_title_to_annotations(), reset_axis_title_text(), add_reference_lines(), add_plot_config(), apply_plotly_newshape(), apply_render_margins(), apply_legend_styling() / apply_legend_inputs(), add_size_legend() (the circle size legend plotly drops when marker size encodes a column, as the DotPlot module and dittoDotPlot draw it; give it the plot’s size-scale limits and size.range so its circles match the points, and breaks to leave out an empty size-0 circle), empty_plot(). A module that renders uniform_legend_inputs_ui() must apply all of it (legend.show, legend.font.family, legend.font.color and the two sizes), and one that renders the shape controls of uniform_plotly_inputs_ui() must call apply_plotly_newshape(); a plot without cartesian axes passes include.shapes = FALSE and include.modebar.buttons = FALSE instead. A figure split into panels (e.g. by split.by) passes facet.by to add_plot_config(), which drops the editable main title, styles its shared axis and panel titles with apply_axis_title_to_annotations(), and swaps the main title inputs for the facet.title.* ones as the split changes (toggle_facet_title_inputs(); a plot that always facets hides main_title_input_ids instead).
    • Statistics: uniform_stats_inputs_ui() / reset_stats_inputs(), compute_pairwise_stats(), create_stat_annotations(), apply_stat_annotations(), stat_bracket_y_max() / stat_bracket_headroom(), note_brackets_skipped(), generate_pair_strings() / parse_pair_strings() / default_stat_pairs().
    • Point highlighting and labels: parse_highlight_values(), apply_highlight_styling(), create_highlight_annotations(), create_selected_annotations(), merge_annotation_sets().
    • Export: collect_source_data(), create_source_download_handler(), draw_to_svg() / draw_to_png().
    • Data tables and expressions: dataFilterUI() / dataFilterServer(), resolve_column_targets(), safe_eval_filter() / validate_expression().
  • For faceted / multi-panel figures, reuse the facet toolkit rather than hand-rolling layout maths: resolve_facet_sharing(), resolve_facet_layout(), apply_facet_subplot_spacing(), build_facet_annotations(), and build_facet_panel_borders().
  • For a new scientific module, create bespoke plotting or module code only when VizModules does not provide an appropriate base. Reuse its input organization, layout, download, and plotly conventions where applicable.
  • Build plots with plotly wherever plotly can do the job - the VizModules helpers this package leans on assume it (see Critical Rule 6 for when a non-plotly widget is acceptable). Do not assume that every argument of an underlying dittoViz, dittoSeq, or plotthis function is exposed through a VizModules module; verify its documented signature first.

Use the VizModules Skills for Module Work

Before adding a module, wrapping a base module, or wiring modules into an app, load the matching VizModules agent skill and follow it. They encode the conventions this file only summarizes (reactive defaults, double-render avoidance, manual-edit persistence, the uniform input helpers, CSS containment), and they are kept in step with each VizModules release. If they are not already in .claude/skills/ (or .agents/skills/, .github/skills/), install them first with VizModules::use_vizmodules_skills(".", client = "claude"), which copies them from the installed VizModules (overwrite = TRUE refreshes them after a VizModules upgrade).

Task in this package Skill
A new module that wraps a VizModules base module (as volcanoPlot, maPlot, doseResponse, enrichmentDotPlot do), or changes to one vizmodules-custom-module
A new standalone module with its own plotting function (as cnSegmentPlot, survivalCurve, goFanPlot and the dittoSeq modules are) vizmodules-custom-module for the module wiring, plus vizmodules-new-module for the InputsUI/OutputUI/Server/App quartet, its roxygen sections, uniform helpers, gallery registration and tests. That skill is written for the VizModules source tree, so map its file and registry steps onto this repo: its .module_showcase(), .module_example(), .example_datasets() and moduleGalleryApp() are this package’s .sci_module_showcase(), .sci_module_example(), .sci_example_catalogue() / .sci_example_dataset() and sciModuleGalleryApp() (all in R/module_showcase.R and R/moduleGallery_app.R), plus _pkgdown.yml. See “Adding a Module: Gallery, App and Figure Builder”
*App() functions, the module gallery (sciModuleGalleryApp()), sciFigureBuilderApp(), defaults / hide.inputs / hide.tabs usage in examples and vignettes vizmodules-app

Where a skill and this file disagree, this file wins on sciVizModules-specific conventions (no LazyData, .sci_debounced_input(), Bioconductor packaging); the skill wins on how VizModules itself behaves.

VizModules Reference Sources

Use these sources before guessing at a VizModules API or adding a replacement helper:

  1. The bundled agent skills. VizModules ships three under inst/skills/, installable into this project with VizModules::use_vizmodules_skills(".", client = "claude") (also "agents" for .agents/skills, "copilot" for .github/skills). Start here - they are written for this job and are far cheaper than reading the vignettes:
    • vizmodules-app - wiring modules into an app: defaults, hide.inputs / hide.tabs, the Stats tab, createModuleApp(), the data filter, the figure builder, source-data export. Its references/module-inventory.md is the generated, authoritative list of every module’s mapping keys, colour key and tab names.
    • vizmodules-custom-module - wrapping or extending a base module, which is what most of this package does. Its references/reactive-and-rerender.md is the canonical write-up of the double-render problem.
    • vizmodules-new-module - authoring a module inside VizModules itself. Its references/css-containment.md and references/uniform-helpers.md apply here too.
  2. Installed package help and vignettes: help(package = "VizModules"), vignette("quick-start", package = "VizModules"), vignette("custom-modules", package = "VizModules"), and vignette("adding-a-new-module", package = "VizModules").
  3. The source itself, which is often checked out alongside this repo at ../VizModules. Reading R/*.R there is the fastest way to confirm exact helper behavior and argument semantics.
  4. Package website and reference: https://j-andrews7.github.io/VizModules/ and https://j-andrews7.github.io/VizModules/reference/. The site carries an llms.txt and a .md beside each page.
  5. Repository: https://github.com/j-andrews7/VizModules.

Check the installed version with packageVersion("VizModules") before relying on a helper; this package tracks it closely and helpers are added often.

Base modules available in VizModules: ComplexHeatmap_Heatmap, dittoViz_freqPlot, dittoViz_scatterPlot, dittoViz_yPlot, dumbbellPlot, linePlot, parallelCoordinatesPlot, piePlot, plotthis_AreaPlot, plotthis_BarPlot, plotthis_BoxPlot, plotthis_DensityPlot, plotthis_DotPlot, plotthis_Histogram, plotthis_SplitBarPlot, radarPlot. Plus two that are not plot modules: dataFilter (the filterable data table) and figureBuilder (a namespaced, embeddable multi-panel figure canvas). Run the matching *App() function to inspect one interactively when useful.

plotthis_ViolinPlot was removed in VizModules 0.5.0 - plotthis rolled its own geom in v0.14.0, which stopped round-tripping through ggplotly(). Use dittoViz_yPlot with defaults = list(plots = "vlnplot") instead (add "boxplot" / "jitter" for the inner box and points).

Do not trust this list over inst/skills/vizmodules-app/references/module-inventory.md in the VizModules source, which is generated and also carries each module’s mapping keys, colour key and tab names.

Avoiding Double Renders

Three situations, three different tools. Picking the wrong one gives a plot that rebuilds twice per change - cheap on a toy dataset, painful on a real one.

  1. A parent app drives a module parameter -> a reactive entry in defaults. Resolved server-side in the same flush as the data, so the plot renders once and the control stays populated and editable. Not update*Input() from the parent, which is an async browser round-trip. Create the store with setup_reactive_defaults(defaults, input, session) as the first statement of moduleServer(), and pass it to setup_auto_update_logic(input, params). Reads must stay in the literal form isolate_fn(input$key), because the wrapper inspects substitute() to decide whether to redirect to the store.
  2. A module updates one of its own ordinary inputs -> freezeReactiveValue() immediately before the update, in the same branch. Never wrap renderPlotly() in a catch-all tryCatch(): the pause arrives as a silent condition, and swallowing it turns a clean pause into a blank plot.
  3. A module updates an input that renderUI() rebuilds -> a server-side store. Freezing cannot help: it pauses only readers that run after it in that flush, and at startup the plot output runs first. Use setup_group_colors() for a multiColorPicker() (seed it inside the renderUI() with the same resolve_palette() result the picker is built from, and read isolate_fn(palette_store()) in the plot) and setup_axis_range() for y-limit controls (seed it beside every update*Input() that sets them).

default_group_colors(defaults, key) validates a caller-supplied mapping before it reaches resolve_palette()’s manual_colors argument, and reset_group_colors() puts the picker back to it on Reset.

Debouncing Free Text

textInput() and textAreaInput() report on every keystroke, so a plot that reads one directly is rebuilt once per character - and for a gene list or an expression, most of those characters are a state the plot cannot use. Use .sci_debounced_input(input, "key", params) (R/input_helpers.R), created once in the module server body; inside another reactive it rebuilds the timer and does nothing. 700ms matches VizModules. Select, numeric, checkbox and slider inputs report discrete choices and need nothing.

CSS Containment

Any stylesheet or inline tags$style() this package ships lands in the host app’s document. There is no shadow DOM and no automatic scoping, and every plot module pulls a colour picker in, so one bare selector restyles an app that merely wanted one plot. VizModules was bitten by this three times (#355).

Anchor every rule on a class this package invents - .scivizmodules- or .sci-. Judge by the leftmost class: if you did not invent it, the rule is not scoped. .navbar, .well, .nav-tabs, .form-group, .selectize-dropdown, .option, .btn and friends are Bootstrap’s, selectize’s or DT’s, not yours.

Layout belongs in a stylesheet, not an inline style= (which a host app can only override with !important); per-instance values go through a CSS custom property. Do not assume the parent’s padding - use gap, and min-width: 0 on flex children. A dropdown or popover parented to <body> cannot be reached by a descendant selector, so give it a marker class of its own.

This package currently ships no package-level CSS; the only stylesheet is the module gallery’s (.sci_gallery_css() in R/moduleGallery_app.R), every rule scoped to .scivizmodules-gallery - tests/testthat/test-module-gallery.R checks that. Keep it that way.

Adding a Module: Gallery, App and Figure Builder

Every module is in the gallery. Its entry in .sci_module_showcase() (R/module_showcase.R) is part of the module, not an afterthought: one entry gives it its gallery tab and Overview card, the example its *App() opens on, and, for a data-frame module, its Figure Builder entry. tests/testthat/test-showcase.R derives the package’s modules from its exports (every X with XInputsUI, XOutputUI, XServer and XApp exported) and fails, naming the module, when one has no entry. So when you add a module:

  1. Add its showcase entry with .sci_showcase_entry(): the module’s base name, its label and shorter tab label, its group (one of .sci_gallery_groups, the gallery’s menus), a one-line description, its dataset, its kind ("df" for a data frame fed through the gallery’s filterable table, "object" for anything else, with a preview function returning a data frame of it), and any Suggests it needs in needs.
  2. Give it showcase defaults that switch on its distinctive features - highlighted genes or variants, statistics, annotation tracks, splits, trajectories, fit lines - not just column mappings. The defaults must name real columns and values and be accepted by the controls they seed; test-showcase.R checks both, so a key no control reads fails as well.
  3. Add a catalogue loader to .sci_example_catalogue() if the module brings new example data (list the Suggests it is read from in needs, and use app_datasets for further datasets its *App() should offer).
  4. Open its *App() on the showcase example: give it defaults = NULL, hide.inputs = NULL, hide.tabs = NULL, and when its data argument is NULL, take example <- .sci_module_example("<id>", defaults) and use example$data_list and example$defaults. Pass defaults, hide.inputs and hide.tabs on to createModuleApp() or the internal app factory, which drop the NULL ones (.sci_server_args()) so a server’s own hide.tabs default survives. Document them with @inheritParams volcanoPlotApp.
  5. Set figure_builder = TRUE if it takes a data frame and renders plotly.
  6. Add it to _pkgdown.yml and to the module list in this file.
  7. Open its tab in sciModuleGalleryApp() and check that it renders as intended on its showcase settings.

Module Structure Pattern

Each module has at least 3 files: *_module_ui.R (InputsUI/OutputUI functions), *_module_server.R (Server function), *_module_app.R (*App() example). A 4th file of module-specific helpers is allowed, e.g. goFanPlot_helpers.R. Standalone plotting functions get their own file, e.g. goFanPlot.R, cnSegmentPlot.R.

Keep the plotting function usable on its own, independent of Shiny. The module server should be a thin layer that maps inputs onto that function’s arguments and then applies the shared VizModules finalize stack.

Where the UI and server both need the same defaults or input choices, factor them into a shared internal helper rather than duplicating the literal in both files — the two drift otherwise (see .cn_seg_base_defaults() and friends in R/cnSegmentPlot.R).

Critical Namespace Pattern for Wrapper Modules

wrapperServer <- function(id, data_reactive) {
    # Process data INSIDE moduleServer to access namespaced inputs
    filtered_data <- moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
        reactive({ /* use input$customField here */ })
    })
    # Call base module OUTSIDE to avoid double-namespacing (id-id-inputName)
    baseModuleServer(id, filtered_data)
}

In UI: Use NS(id) for wrapper’s inputs, pass bare id to base module UI functions.

Documentation Requirements

  • All exports need complete roxygen2 docs with @param, @return, @export, @author, @examples
  • Internal helpers use @keywords internal with a @rdname INTERNAL_* alias
  • Reference the underlying dittoViz / dittoSeq / plotthis parameters where applicable
  • Document missing/broken plotly functionality explicitly
  • Do not update NEWS.md while the package is at its initial version (0.99.0, pre-Bioconductor release). Its entries describe that first release as a whole, so fixes and changes to unreleased modules do not get their own bullets

Code Style

4-space indent, 120 char max line, tidyverse style guide, roxygen markdown enabled (Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE)).

Dependencies

Depends: R (>= 4.6.0), shiny, VizModules (>= 0.6.0)

Imports: colourpicker, dittoSeq, DT, GenomicRanges, ggplot2, IRanges, jsonlite, methods, NGLVieweR, plotly, readxl, S4Vectors, scales, Seqinfo, shinyBS, shinyjqui, shinyjs, shinyWidgets, SingleCellExperiment, stats, SummarizedExperiment, survival

Suggests: airway, circlize, ComplexHeatmap, DESeq2, drc, edgeR, fgsea, GOfan, htmltools, InteractiveComplexHeatmap, knitr, maftools, org.Hs.eg.db, PCAtools, PKNCA, pROC, rmarkdown, sesame, sesameData, survminer, testthat (>= 3.0.0)

Keep Imports: and NAMESPACE in step in both directions - R CMD check and BiocCheck flag an undeclared import and an unused declaration alike. Several packages resolve at runtime only because VizModules Depends: on them; that is not a declaration.

Bioconductor packages appear throughout; some example data depends on sesame/sesameData, goFanPlot needs GOfan plus an OrgDb, and doseResponse needs drc. PCAtools is needed only to build a pca object and for the scree plot’s elbow marker. pROC supplies the DeLong AUC interval in rocCurve; pROC, PKNCA and fgsea are otherwise test references for quantities computed in-package, as survminer is for survivalCurve‘s pairwise log-rank tests. The heatmap modules (dittoHeatmap, sampleDistanceHeatmap, deHeatmap) need ComplexHeatmap, InteractiveComplexHeatmap and circlize; DESeq2 supplies the variance-stabilising transformation of the bulk modules; maftools supplies mutationLollipop’s protein domains and the example MAF (its TCGA LAML cohort, read by .maf_example()), and with edgeR is otherwise a test reference; airway supplies the bulk modules’ example experiment (.se_example()). All are Suggests and must be reached through requireNamespace() and guarded in examples and tests.

Common Issues

Issue Solution
“object not exported by namespace” Run devtools::document() to regenerate NAMESPACE
document() rewrites the whole NAMESPACE DESCRIPTION records Config/roxygen2/version. A newer installed roxygen2 reformats every entry and bumps the stamp. Keep the diff scoped: revert the unrelated hunks, or agree to the reformat deliberately rather than as a side effect
Linting failures Check .lintr: 120 char lines, 4-space indents
“Non-standard file/directory” in check Add to .Rbuildignore with regex pattern
Module inputs not responding Namespace issue - verify NS(id) pattern (see above)
Vignette build errors Install: install.packages(c("knitr", "rmarkdown"))
'scattergl' objects don't have these attributes: 'hoveron' Benign plotly warning from toWebGL() on line traces; noisy in test output, not a failure
Faceted figure loses its draggable axis titles axis_titles_as_annotations() intentionally skips multi-panel figures; use apply_axis_title_to_annotations() instead
“object ‘example_sce’ not found” in package code No LazyData, so bundled datasets are not promises in the namespace. Use .sci_example_data("example_sce"); in an @examples block or a test, call data() first
A plot renders two or three times for one change See “Avoiding Double Renders” above - pick the right one of reactive defaults, freezeReactiveValue(), or a server-side store
shiny::testServer() cannot drive a plotly output Expected; assert on the server’s own reactives instead, or verify structurally with plotly::plotly_build()
test-showcase.R fails with “No gallery showcase entry for: …” A module was added without its gallery entry. Add one to .sci_module_showcase() and open its *App() on it (see “Adding a Module: Gallery, App and Figure Builder”)
A showcase default “does nothing” get_default() drops a value its control rejects and ignores a key no control reads; test-showcase.R reports both. Check the key against the module’s *InputsUI() docs
Shiny server has sent a progress message ... unexpected state in the browser console Comes from the VizModules scatter module under Shiny 1.14 and shows in its standalone apps too; not caused by the gallery

Critical Rules

  1. Build upon VizModules whenever possible - start from an existing VizModules module or helper; add only the scientific specialization this package owns. Verify the installed API before calling it.
  2. NEVER edit NAMESPACE manually - always use devtools::document()
  3. ALWAYS run devtools::document() after changing roxygen2 comments or signatures
  4. Run devtools::test() after changes to verify the testthat test suite passes; also test modules interactively via example apps
  5. Follow namespace pattern strictly for wrapper modules (see Coding Conventions)
  6. Strongly prefer plotly - the shared finishing helpers, manual-edit persistence, the Figure Builder and the source-data images all assume a plotly figure, so a module built from scratch should be plotly unless plotly has no reasonable equivalent. A non-plotly htmlwidget with Shiny bindings is acceptable in that case (e.g. a 3D molecular viewer via NGLVieweR or r3dmol; VizModules’ own ComplexHeatmap_Heatmap is another). Such a module must say so in its docs, and supply its own image export. To appear in the Figure Builder export and source archive it needs vector_svg / raster_png renderers (built with draw_to_svg() / draw_to_png()); without them it contributes no artwork there
  7. Document missing features - clearly note functionality unavailable in plotly
  8. Use VizModules::organize_inputs() helper for consistent UI layouts
  9. Keep changes scoped - do not let generated-file churn (NAMESPACE reformatting, roxygen version bumps) ride along with a behavioral change
  10. Every module select is a viz_select_input() - never shiny::selectInput(). A column of gene names is unusable otherwise, and two VizModules 0.5.0 fixes land only on the virtual select. tests/testthat/test-select-inputs.R enforces this
  11. Scope every CSS selector on a class this package invents (see “CSS Containment”)
  12. Load the matching VizModules skill before module work - adding, wrapping or wiring a module starts from vizmodules-custom-module, vizmodules-new-module or vizmodules-app (see “Use the VizModules Skills for Module Work”)
  13. Every module is in the gallery - a new module ships with its .sci_module_showcase() entry, showcase defaults that switch on its distinctive features, and an *App() that opens on them (see “Adding a Module: Gallery, App and Figure Builder”). tests/testthat/test-showcase.R enforces this

Best Practices

  • Avoid sapply usage, it is unsafe in package code. Prefer vapply with an explicit FUN.VALUE.
  • When changing a shared plotting function, keep existing single-input behavior byte-identical unless the change is the point; the existing tests are the regression guard and should stay green untouched.
  • Prefer verifying plotly output structurally (plotly::plotly_build(), then inspect x$data / x$layout) over eyeballing; reserve interactive checks for layout and legibility questions that structure cannot answer.

These instructions are a starting point, not an authority. Verify against the code before relying on any specific claim here, and correct this file when you find it stale.
